To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified potent inhibitors of neuronal NOS, which are highly selective over endothelial and inducible NOS.
a new series of dipeptide amide inhibitors of neuronal nitric oxide synthases have been discovered.

the dipeptide ArgNO2-Dbu-NHNH2 (23), which contains a nitroarginine moiety and a basic amine as the side chains of the two amino acid residues, was found to be the best nNOS inhibitor (Ki = 0.13 μM), and it was also the most selective (over eNOS, 1 500-fold and over iNOS, 200-fold) inhibitor in the series.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of dipeptide amide derivatives of nitroarginine, which have been shown to inhibit nNOS with excellent potency and selectivity over eNO and iNOS.
the development of inhibitors of nitric oxide synthesis, which is the enzyme responsible for the production of nitric oxide.
the design and synthesis of dipeptide amide analogues of the endogenous NO synthase inhibitor, L-arginine, as potential inhibitors of the neuronal form of nitric oxide synthesis (nNOS).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nNOS inhibitors reported here are the most potent and selective inhibitors reported to date.
the dipeptide nitroarginines are potent and selective inhibitors of neuronal nitric oxide synthases and may serve as lead compounds for the design of new inhibitors of this isoform of NOS.

the dipeptide nitroarginine-containing amides are excellent inhibitors of neuronal NOS, and that the best of these compounds (l-ArgNO2-d-Dbu-NHEt (20) and l-ArgNO-d-Dbu-OMe (23)) are potent and highly selective inhibitors of nNOS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have discovered potent and selective nNOS inhibitors that are based on a dipeptide amide scaffold.
the nNOS isoform of nitric oxide synthatase (NOS), which is responsible for the production of nitric oxide in neuronal tissues, can be selectively inhibited by the dipeptide nitroarginine amides.

we have synthesized a large library of Nω-nitroarginine-containing dipeptide amide inhibitors of nNOS and that the best of these inhibitors exhibit potent inhibitory potency and excellent selectivity over the isoforms of NOS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have discovered potent and highly selective nNOS inhibitors.
dipeptide amide inhibitors of nNOS are highly effective and that the selectivity for n- over e- or i-NOS can be enhanced by incorporating a basic side chain in the second position of the dipeptide.
we have discovered potent, selective nNOS inhibitors that are amenable to further modification and optimization.
